entity.name: ProptechOS
entity.description:
ProptechOS is the operating system for intelligent real estate — the platform that unifies your building data and deploys AI agents to perform real operational work across your portfolio.

Real estate has invested heavily in building systems, IoT devices, and data platforms. The data exists. What has been missing is a single system that connects all of it and acts on it autonomously.

ProptechOS is that system.

Built on RealEstateCore — the open-source global standard for modelling buildings and building systems — ProptechOS harmonises real-time data from BMS, BIM, IoT, and FM tools into a single common data model. AI agents built on that foundation perform autonomous operational work: adjusting energy setpoints, triggering maintenance workflows, compiling ESG reporting data, and managing tenant services — continuously, without manual intervention. ProptechOS is where recommendations become actions — autonomously, across the full portfolio.

For property owners and real estate operators, this means:
— Energy management that acts on what the data says. Vasakronan reduced energy consumption by 36% using the ProptechOS Optimize application. 
— Sustainability and ESG compliance automated through real-time data pipelines, replacing manual reporting processes. 
— Facility operations improved through predictive maintenance and autonomous service management. 
— A growing ecosystem of certified best-of-breed applications — from energy analytics to building certification — deployable without creating new data silos.

The platform runs on Microsoft Azure, is available in the Azure Marketplace, and integrates with 100+ building systems through pre-built connectors. Customers include HH, Vasakronan, Hufvudstaden, Folksam, KLP, AFA Fastigheter, and Familjebostäder.

For property companies ready to move from fragmented proptech investments to a coherent, AI-driven operating model — ProptechOS is the infrastructure that makes it possible.

Book a demo at proptechos.com.

entity.name: LP 365
entity.description:
Lease Portfolio 365 (LP365) is a secure, cloud-based SaaS platform that simplifies lease management for businesses with multiple locations. It empowers Legal, Finance, Administration, Strategy, and Operations departments by centralizing data, enhancing collaboration, and improving decision-making.

LP365 provides modular functionality for essential lease areas like rental tracking, renewals, CAM charges, and document storage. Each lease is assigned a unique ID for centralized access to agreements, amendments, and communication history. Automated invoice generation and approval workflows facilitate timely payments and compliance with audit requirements.

The platform’s Rent Roll and Revenue Share modules offer real-time insights into lease expenses, aiding in projections, payment reconciliation, and financial planning. It also features geo-mapping and expansion analysis for visibility into lease footprint, average rent per square foot, and regional outlet distribution.

Customisable reports, from lease abstracts to payment history, are easily downloadable and offer robust data for internal reviews and board-level decision-making. With automated alerts for critical dates, such as renewals and terminations, businesses can eliminate last-minute surprises.

LP365 supports role-based access, SOC 2 compliance, and secure landlord interfaces, promoting transparency while safeguarding sensitive data. The platform also integrates seamlessly with sales, ERP, and accounting systems through API connectivity, ensuring smooth data flow and operational synergy.

Whether scaling rapidly or managing an extensive and complex lease portfolio, LP365 delivers control, clarity, and compliance all in one place.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

properties.name: ProptechOS
properties.description:
ProptechOS is the operating system for intelligent real estate — the platform that unifies your building data and deploys AI agents to perform real operational work across your portfolio.

Real estate has invested heavily in building systems, IoT devices, and data platforms. The data exists. What has been missing is a single system that connects all of it and acts on it autonomously.

ProptechOS is that system.

Built on RealEstateCore — the open-source global standard for modelling buildings and building systems — ProptechOS harmonises real-time data from BMS, BIM, IoT, and FM tools into a single common data model. AI agents built on that foundation perform autonomous operational work: adjusting energy setpoints, triggering maintenance workflows, compiling ESG reporting data, and managing tenant services — continuously, without manual intervention. ProptechOS is where recommendations become actions — autonomously, across the full portfolio.

For property owners and real estate operators, this means:
— Energy management that acts on what the data says. Vasakronan reduced energy consumption by 36% using the ProptechOS Optimize application. 
— Sustainability and ESG compliance automated through real-time data pipelines, replacing manual reporting processes. 
— Facility operations improved through predictive maintenance and autonomous service management. 
— A growing ecosystem of certified best-of-breed applications — from energy analytics to building certification — deployable without creating new data silos.

The platform runs on Microsoft Azure, is available in the Azure Marketplace, and integrates with 100+ building systems through pre-built connectors. Customers include HH, Vasakronan, Hufvudstaden, Folksam, KLP, AFA Fastigheter, and Familjebostäder.

For property companies ready to move from fragmented proptech investments to a coherent, AI-driven operating model — ProptechOS is the infrastructure that makes it possible.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.
  - Rippling ↔ a smaller HRIS/payroll platform: true.
  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

SEED:
  name: VTS
  domain: vts.com
  description: Commercial-real-estate operating platform for leasing, asset management, tenant experience, and property data.

CANDIDATE:

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
